what: The compute_uwshcu_inv surrogate (340 k-parameter MLP with the packed subset block, uwshcu_h256_notr_2cap_sub.pt) timed offline on one A100 against one CPU thread of the same node, at the hook's granularity (16 columns a call, arrays in host memory, the packed output back in host memory) and in larger batches; float64 in and out.  Not a model run: an offline measurement deciding whether a GPU path for the hook is worth building.
node: one Derecho GPU node (main queue, select=1:ncpus=8:ngpus=1:gpu_type=a100)
inputs_from: one captured call of rank 0 (pausable-p29-uwshcu-capture-7493241), padded to 16 columns; batches stack consecutive captured calls
in_image_reference: FTorch on the CPU nodes, 128 ranks a node sharing memory bandwidth: 4.17 ms a call live over the month (7510379)
conclusion: At one chunk a call the A100 is slower than one CPU thread (1.03 ms with the copies, 0.63 ms resident, against 0.60 ms): the call is launch-latency bound.  The GPU pays only from about a thousand columns a call (1 us a column at 4 096, 0.26 us at 16 384 against 7 us on the CPU thread), which the hook never has; it would need the node's ranks to batch their chunks and wait for each other.  Not built.
